Moreover, the ionic diffusion coefficients also vary across the four electrolytes. As illustrated in Fig. 2i, the simulated self-diffusion coefficient of Na $^{+}$ in G1 (1.251×10 $^{-5}$ cm $^{2}$ s $^{-1}$ ) is higher than those in G2 (4.829×10 $^{-6}$ cm $^{2}$ s $^{-1}$ ), G3 (2.210×10 $^{-6}$ cm $^{2}$ s $^{-1}$ ), and G4 (1.525×10 $^{-6}$ cm $^{2}$ s $^{-1}$ ), which aligns with the conductivity measurements shown in Fig. S7. In summary, glyme-based electrolytes with shorter chain lengths facilitate rapid de-solvation and efficient ionic diffusion (Fig. 2j), thus enhancing interfacial kinetics and promoting the formation of an anion-derived SEI, thereby contributing to improved electrochemical performance of the target electrode [7,25]. The above MD simulations, complemented by characterizations, have shed light on the nuanced interplay between sodium ion and solvents, and this interplay consequently affects the coordination structures in electrolytes. Predominantly, these coordination structures can be segmented into three distinct categories based on the proximity of cations to an anion: solvent-separated ion pairs (SSIP) with no cations in the immediate solvation shell, contact ion pairs (CIP) involving a single cation, and aggregates (AGG) where the anion associates with multiple cations [6].

citations.quote: Fig. 3c-f present high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images of HC electrodes after cycling in different electrolyte to observe their SEI layers. It is found that the transparent coating layers can be observed on all the electrode surface, in contrast to the smooth surface of HC shown in Fig. S9, indicates the formation of SEI layers [28]. The SEI layers generated in G1 and G2 are notably more uniform and exhibit closer contact with the HC surface compared to those generated in G3 and G4. This enhanced uniformity and adherence provides effective protection for the electrode and ensure stable electrochemical performance for sodium storage [29,30]. To ascertain the chemical composition of the SEI layers, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses were performed on cycled HC electrodes. Variations in peak intensities and binding energies were analyzed to distinguish the inorganic and organic components of the SEI layers formed in different electrolytes. Fig. 3g displays the C 1 s, O 1 s, and F 1 s spectra of the SEI layer formed in G1. Deconvolution of the C 1 s spectrum reveals four peaks at approximately 289.4 (RCO₃), 286.3 (C=O), 283.8 (C-O), and 283.4 (C-C/C-H) eV, indicative of decomposed products of sodium salts, solvent-induced polymerizations, polyethylene oxide oligomers, and polyolefin, respectively [11,31].

citations.quote: The HC//NFPP full cell shows stable cycling performance over 100 cycles with a high average CE (Figure S12, Supporting Information), indicating the high combability of the NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte in the full cells. An Ah-level HC//NFPP pouch cells were further assembled to test the feasibility of the practical application of the NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte. The HC//NFPP pouch cell delivers a reversible capacity of 1.029 Ah and ICE of 82.5% (Figure 3a). Meanwhile, the pouch cell exhibits excellent cycling stability with no swelling during the cycling process. Specifically, the pouch cell manifests a high capacity retention of 80% after 500 cycles at a current rate of 1 C, along with a high average CE of 99.9% (Figure 3b). Moreover, the pouch cell shows stable performance at different temperatures. The discharge capacities are 0.985, 0.884, and 1.06 Ah at -20, -40, and 60 °C (0.1 C), corresponding to 95.7%, 85.9%, and 103% of the capacity retention, respectively (Figure 3c). Even at a higher discharge rate of 0.5 C at 60 °C, the battery can still maintain 103% of its capacity at 25 °C (Figure S13, Supporting Information). The HC//NFPP pouch cell shows outstanding cycling stability at -20 and 60 °C with high capacity retention over hundreds of cycles (Figure 3d,e; Figure S14, Supporting Information). These results indicated the high combability of NaDFOB-G2 electrolytes for practical pouch cells.

To show the potential for low-temperature application, the NFPP electrodes with different electrolytes were tested at low temperatures. Notably, the NFPP electrode with NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte exhibits a capacity retention of 92.7% at -20 °C compared to that at 25 °C. Even at -40 °C, a high capacity retention of 84.8% is achieved (Figure 2g,h). Impressively, the NFPP electrode with the NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte retains higher capacity retention than that with $NaPF_{6}-G2$ electrolyte at both -20 and -40 °C (Figures S6 and S7, Supporting Information). Moreover, the NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte works well with other cathode materials. Both the $\mathrm{Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}}$ and $\mathrm{Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{2}F_{3}}$ electrodes show high cycling stability over 200 cycles (Figures S8 and S9, Supporting Information). Additionally, the compatibility of the NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte with the hard carbon (HC) anode is also evaluated. The HC electrode has a large overpotential at room temperature and shows a small capacity (Figure S10, Supporting Information), which may be result of the thick SEI film on the Na metal surface slowing down the speed of sodium-ions passing through the SEI film and increase the polarization of the cell (Figure S11, Supporting Information). $^{[8]}$

To avoid the influence of the high polarization from Na metal, HC//NFPP full coin-cells were assembled.

citations.quote: In summary, we developed a synthetic strategy combining a molten-salt method with a vacuum infiltration process to successfully construct a $Nb_{0.03}$ -NC composite with an $Nb-N_{4}$ coordination structure, which was employed as an anode for SIBs. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that $NaPF_{6}$ in an ether-based electrolyte (DME) more effectively promotes the electrochemical performance of electrode materials compared to ester-based electrolytes. The $Nb-N_{4}$ configuration regulates the microstructure and charge distribution of NC, significantly enhancing the pseudocapacitive behavior of $Na^{+}$ storage and enabling fast reaction kinetics. Further investigations and DFT calculations reveal the storage mechanism: the $Nb-N_{4}$ structure promotes the formation of a stable, uniform SEI layer rich in inorganic NaF by lowering the dissociation energy of P—F and C—O bonds in the $NaPF_{6}$ -DME electrolyte, thereby improving specific capacity, rate performance, and cycling stability at both room and low temperatures. The optimized $Nb_{0.03}$ -NC exhibits remarkable cycling stability of 238 mAh g $^{-1}$ surpassing 3000 cycles at 10 C (25°C) and exceptional low-temperature capacity of 203 mAh g $^{-1}$ (0°C) and 130 mAh g $^{-1}$ (-20°C) at 2 C. In practical applications, a full cell assembled with NVPF cathode and $Nb_{0.03}$ -NC anode achieves an energy density of 230 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and a power density of 6.69 kW kg $^{-1}$ .

The LUMO value of the DME solvent is 1.17 eV, which is higher than those of the ester solvents EC (–0.40 eV), EMC (–0.07 eV), and DMC (–0.14 eV). Figure 2d and Figure S12 illustrate the electrostatic potentials and weak interaction distributions of molecules in the $NaPF_{6}$ -DME and $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/EMC/DMC electrolyte systems. Regions in red represent relatively positive electrostatic potentials, while blue indicates relatively negative (electron-rich) regions, reflecting localized charge accumulation. In the $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/EMC/DMC system, the electrostatic potential range of EMC ranges from -1.59 eV (blue, negative charge) to 1.09 eV (red, positive charge). The non-uniform distribution of polar groups leads to charge inhomogeneity, which can alter the solvation structure of $Na^{+}$ and affect the ion migration energy barrier. In contrast, the electrostatic potential range of DME in the $NaPF_{6}$ -DME system ranges from -1.48 eV (blue, negative charge) to 0.81 eV (red, positive charge). Compared with ester-based solvents, DME exhibits a much smaller variation in electrostatic potential and a more homogeneous charge distribution.

citations.quote: Compared with ester-based solvents, DME exhibits a much smaller variation in electrostatic potential and a more homogeneous charge distribution. This likely results in a looser solvation structure, thereby reducing the desolvation energy barrier for $Na^{+}$ and facilitating faster interfacial ion transport [28]. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were employed to calculate the average coordination number of $Na^{+}$ in the ether-based and ester-based electrolytes (Figure 2e–g). According to the radial distribution function (RDF) analysis, in the $NaPF_{6}$ in EC/EMC/DMC system, $Na^{+}$ preferentially coordinates with the oxygen atoms (O) of the solvents (EC/EMC/DMC), forming an inner solvation sheath. The coordination numbers are 2.46 for EC, 1.50 for EMC, and 1.35 for DMC, indicating that ion-solvent interactions dominate. In the DME-based electrolyte, $Na^{+}$ also coordinates with oxygen atoms, but with a higher coordination number of 4.74. The number of $PF_{6}^{-}$ anions around $Na^{+}$ was determined from the RDF between $Na^{+}$ and F (in $PF_{6}^{-}$ ). Within a distance of r = 0.23 nm, there are approximately $0.85\;PF_{6}^{-}$ anions coordinated to $Na^{+}$ in the ester-based electrolyte, compared to 1.25 $PF_{6}^{-}$ anions in the ether-based electrolyte. This indicates stronger Na–F interactions between $PF_{6}^{-}$ and $Na^{+}$ in the latter system.

citations.quote:
4. CONCLUSIONS
In summary, the incorporation of PFPN as an electrolyte additive has successfully led to significant enhancements in both the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries and the flame retardancy of the electrolyte. The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a SEI layer rich in P and N elements on the electrode surface. The SEI layer is thinner and possesses superior kinetic properties compared to the baseline, effectively preventing sodium plating and enhancing the cycle life. This research highlights the potential of PFPN in sodium ion battery applications requiring long-life and low-temperature operation, offering new insights into electrolyte modification using P- and F-containing additives.

citations.quote: Despite significant advancements in the use of phosphorus-containing electrolytes and additives in laboratory research, their specific mechanisms of action in practical batteries remain poorly understood. $^{25,26}$ This knowledge gap highlights the need for further research to elucidate the mechanisms of performance enhancement by phosphorus-containing components, especially in SIBs, which is critical for advancing their commercialization. $^{27}$ Among these components, ethoxy (pentafluoro) cyclotriphosphazene (PFPN) has been widely utilized as an additive to enhance battery safety. $^{28,29}$ In this study, PFPN was introduced into practical pouch-cell-type SIBs to evaluate its effects on cycling performance and capacity optimization under various temperature conditions, thereby redefining the application potential of PFPN additives. These results demonstrate that PFPN significantly improves the low-temperature electrochemical performance of SIBs. Specifically, the incorporation of 10 wt % PFPN enables the battery to retain 85% of its initial capacity after 450 cycles at a 0.2 C rate at 0 °C. During electrochemical cycling, PFPN facilitates the formation of a unique SEI layer enriched with phosphorus and nitrogen elements, which improves the kinetic performance of the battery.

Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries.    用现有 `evidence_claim` 表达候选须有相应工况下的直接测试依据，而非把近似目标
   改成精确相等、单边不等式或自行设定容差。逐候选判断时，`supported` 须引用该
   候选的实际测试条件与性能原句，`basis` 写清实测条件与目标的差别及其关联依据。
   只有其他工况的结果、测试建议或机理预测时，不能据此判近似工况要求已满足。
   没有相应测试依据就保留 `not_found` 并补证，不能删掉该要求后批准推荐，再把它
   放进 `next_steps`。有邻近条件下的直接依据时，在报告中明确实际条件与目标的
   差别，精确目标下的后续验证可以另列。电极、电池形式和其他明确要求仍须检查。
   联合条件也须保留近似目标的含义：不得把近似值写成 `target_context` 中要求
   精确匹配的数值。近似工况及其电极、全电池归属可写在同一 `evidence_claim`
   中，引用实际共同测试的结果；组分身份等与工况无关的要求不并入该测试条件组。
   “低成本”等定性目标须区分文献提出的成本动机与已量化的价格优势；未提供价格数据
   时不得称已验证低成本。数值明确的用户要求仍按原值建立硬约束，不得因此放宽。
   无法从问题得出数值判据的定性目标，保留为选材目标，在报告中说明依据和待验证
   条件。定性或近似目标通过断言及其原文依据判断，不变成必须命中字面词的关键词条件。
   这不允许省略用户明确给出的电极、电池形式、精确温度或倍率要求。
   当用户目标包含某项性能指标（如 capacity retention relative to room-temperature
   capacity、离子电导率、倍率性能、首圈库仑效率），先分清用户给的是**数值阈值**还是
   **只要报告**：给了明确数值时写成对应数值约束——保持率用 `minimum_retention`、
   电导率用 `minimum_conductivity`、倍率用 `c_rate`，`value` 取用户给出的数值；
   只要求“报告该指标”“有无该结果”而未给数值时，不得把阈值填 0 了事——`value: 0`
   会让任何数字都通过，等于没有检查。这类“须被报告/须成立”的指标改用
   `kind: "evidence_claim"`（见下），把该指标写成一句断言。
   `field_presence` 只用于检查候选的配方字段（`concentration_mol_l`、
   `solvent_ratios`、`additives` 等）是否显式填写，绝不用于表达“某项性能必须被报告”。
   禁止把“capacity retention … must be reported”写成
   `"kind": "field_presence", "field": "additives"` 这类把性能指标错配到配方字段的约束。
   ```json
   {
     "request": {
       "candidates": candidates,
       "constraint_records": [
         {
           "constraint_id": "temp-low",
           "description": "operating temperature ≤ -20°C",
           "kind": "temperature",
           "operator": "<=",
           "value": -20,
           "unit": "°C",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find low-temperature cycling evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "electrode-hard-carbon",
           "description": "hard carbon anode",
           "kind": "electrode_material",
           "evidence_terms": ["hard carbon", "hard-carbon"],
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find hard carbon anode evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "cell-half",
           "description": "sodium half-cell configuration",
           "kind": "cell_configuration",
           "evidence_terms": ["half-cell", "half cell", "Na||HC", "HC||Na", "pure Na"],
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find half-cell configuration evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "field-concentration",
           "description": "explicit salt concentration must be present",
           "kind": "field_presence",
           "field": "concentration_mol_l",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": false
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "salt-napf6",
           "description": "NaPF6 as salt",
           "kind": "required_component",
           "value": "NaPF6",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find NaPF6 electrolyte evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "solvent-thf",
           "description": "THF as solvent",
           "kind": "required_component",
           "value": "THF",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find THF solvent evidence"
         }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```
   定性或断言型要求（如“无集流体/壳体腐蚀被观测到”“无析钠/无枝晶”“提高首圈库仑效率”
   “该添加剂抑制产气”）不得写成 `mechanism_keyword` 关键词表——关键词命中分不清
   “发生腐蚀”与“未发生腐蚀”。改用 `kind: "evidence_claim"`：在 `claim` 里用一句
   用户原话写出对单个候选须成立的断言，在 `claim_verdicts` 里**逐候选**给出判定。
   语义判断（这段原文是否为该候选建立或推翻该断言）由你负责；程序只做两件可机械
   核验的事：判定须指向本次请求的候选，`quote` 须在该候选证据正文中逐字存在。
   因此措辞、否定、同义称呼的变化都不影响判定，你只需如实读原文：
   - `supported`：有原文明确为该候选建立断言，附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `refuted`：有原文明确反驳（如原文说“会持续腐蚀铝箔”），附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `not_found`：检索到的证据未直接提及，如实填写，由补证机制驱动下一轮检索。
   背景介绍、他人体系的结果、无实验支撑的预测都不算 `supported`。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "constraint_id": "no-corrosion",
     "description": "no current-collector or case corrosion observed",
     "kind": "evidence_claim",
     "claim": "该候选电解液不腐蚀铝箔或钢壳",
     "claim_verdicts": [
       {
         "candidate_id": "candidate-1",
         "verdict": "refuted",
         "chunk_id": "fan2024::sec3",
         "quote": "the single NaFSI system can continuously corrode aluminum foil and stainless steel sheets",
         "basis": "原文明确说明单盐 NaFSI 会持续腐蚀铝箔与不锈钢，与该断言相反。"
       }
     ],
     "can_replan": true,
     "search_hint": "find corrosion test evidence for the candidate electrolyte"
   }
   ```
   `evidence_claim` 不得把 `required_evidence_scope` 设为 `component` 或 `background`：
   断言必须由候选自身绑定的证据支持，不能借用别篇论文或背景段落的措辞。
   给出 `supported` 前，逐句核对引文是否真正支持所写断言。引文必须从指定
   `chunk_id` 返回的原文复制，不能把题名、摘要或另一块文字放在该块的标识下。
   配方、测试条件和性能必须对应同一候选；一种优点不能替代另一项目标的证据。
   成本动机与价格比较分别表述，安全性或无氟组成不能自行推导出成本优势。
   `basis` 说明原句与断言的推理关系，不得以重复断言代替理由。程序核验引文
   存在及归属，不代替科学含义判断；证据未支持完整断言时应补证或保留 `not_found`。
   `criteria`/`target_conditions` 仅用于兼容旧调用方；新设计任务必须优先使用
   `constraint_records`，避免 evaluator 再从自由文本猜测硬约束。

   `required_evidence_kinds` 描述的是**支持记录本身的语义角色**，不是实验条件元数据。
   数值性能约束通常只要求 `property`；温度、电极、循环数等共同实例化条件应由该
   observation 的 `condition_scope` 和 `joint_context_requirements` 表达。除非硬约束本身
   确实要求一条独立的 condition 记录，否则不要把同一数值约束写成
   `required_evidence_kinds=["property", "condition"]`，否则会把“带条件上下文的性能观测”
   错当成缺少第二种证据角色。

   当两个及以上硬约束必须在**同一个目标实验上下文**中同时成立时，还必须显式写
   `joint_context_requirements`。分别在多个倍率测试的要求，按倍率分别建立条件组，
   每组的 `target_context.rate` 只填一个倍率。不能把 `0.5 C and 1 C` 当成一次测试的倍率。
   同一论文的不同盐浓度或溶剂比例必须分别对应其性能段，不能因来自同篇论文就互换结果。
   `target_context.cell_configuration` 使用条件检查器的外形名称 `pouch` 或 `coin`，
   不拼成 `pouch full cell` 这样的新标签。全电池要求另用 cell_configuration 检查条件
   和明确的正负极对验证；外形名称不能代替电极与全电池要求。
   它描述的是 evidence composition obligation，不要求所有
   支持证据拥有相同 `experiment_id`。`constraint_ids` 只能引用本次 `constraint_records`；
   `context_fields` 只列对联合决策真正相关的字段；`target_context` 只填写用户明确给出的
   目标条件，未知字段保持未知，禁止为了让 join 成立而补默认值。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "joint_context_requirements": [
       {
         "group_id": "low-temp-high-voltage",
         "constraint_ids": ["retention", "voltage"],
         "context_fields": ["temperature_c", "electrode"],
         "target_context": {"temperature_c": -20.0, "electrode": "hard carbon"},
         "can_replan": true,
         "search_hint": "find evidence satisfying both hard constraints at the target operating context"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```
   只有约束确实需要共同实例化时才声明 joint group；互不相关的硬约束不要强行合组。
   原文条件检查器分别识别 `electrode` 与 `cell_configuration`。涉及电池形式的用户要求
   使用独立的 cell_configuration 条件；只有相关观测明确提供该字段时，才作联合检查。
2. 检查用户输入与已有 ledger；存在组分、机理或替代体系缺口时，选择相应检索能力；
3. 如证据不足，再做有界补充检索：
   - 区分“已有候选缺少一段证据”和“已有候选并不适合目标”。先检查最相关论文；
     若当前候选仍不能满足目标，按缺口与完整目标检索其他候选，不反复只查原来的
     盐、溶剂或论文。新证据支持新的组成时重新组装候选，再用原任务的全部条件
     筛选。不能把不同候选的成本、工况或性能拼成一个通过的候选。
   - 尚未定位候选论文时，用 `search_literature_chunks` 做 1–2 次聚焦补充（`top_k=10`）；
   - 若返回结果已经给出明确 `paper_id`，且该论文与目标组分/机理直接相关但缺少显式配方或目标工况证据，必须对最相关的 1 篇论文调用一次 `search_paper_chunks(paper_id=..., query=..., top_k=8)`；`query` 用 4–8 个英文技术词描述缺失事实，不含作者名。将结果追加到 `evidence_chunks`，不得跨论文拼接配方与性能。
   - 对 **named-study / named-candidate** 设计任务，在进入 `query_formulation_space` 或
     `screen_formulations` 前，必须先取得同一论文中可追溯的配方/组成证据：至少有一条
     `evidence_kind="formulation"` 的记录能支持候选的盐、溶剂或添加剂组成。只有性能、温度、
     机理 chunk 不能建立候选配方归属；若当前只找到性能证据，应继续检索 formulation /
     composition 段落，而不是手工构造一个 `formulation_evidence_ids=[]` 的候选进入筛选。
4. 用户没有提供可评估候选时，调用 `query_formulation_space`，把目标转成：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","target_conditions":[...],"preferred_salts":[...],"preferred_solvents":[...],"preferred_additives":[...],"excluded_components":[...],"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"max_candidates":3}}`；其中 `evidence_chunks` 必须传入前面检索实际返回、与目标最相关的最多 12 个 chunk，不得只传组分偏好而丢失文献上下文。工具会优先从这些同论文原文块组装候选，再使用 KG fallback；保留工具原样返回的 `candidates`。
   如果候选 evidence 只有 `chunk_id` 而 `text/excerpt` 为空，先调用
   `enrich_formulation_evidence({"request":{"candidates": candidates}})`，并用返回候选
   替换原列表；证据已有原文时不得为形式完整重复调用。enrichment 只补齐原文和元数据，
   必须保留原 evidence 的 `paper_id`、`evidence_kind` 和 `chunk_id`。
5. 若任务涉及离子电导率、温度下的传输性质或需要在多个 NaPF6–EC/EMC/PC 候选之间增加一个轻量定量参考，可在筛选前调用 `predict_formulation_conductivity`。只有以下两种情况允许数值预测：候选已有明确的 NaPF6/EC/EMC/PC 摩尔组成，或调用参数中的 `composition_inputs[candidate_id]` 显式给出 `component_mmol`、`molar_ratios` 或 `x_NaSalt/x_EC/x_PC`。现有 `solvent_ratios` 没有保存 v/v、w/w 或 molar 基准，因此**不得**仅凭“1 M + 1:1”之类字段推导模型输入。含其他盐、其他溶剂或添加剂的候选按域外处理；组成不足时保留 `insufficient_composition`，继续依赖文献/KG 证据。`model_predictions` 与 literature evidence 必须分开：模型预测可以辅助候选比较和后续实验优先级，但不能单独把实验事实型硬约束判为满足。
6. 只有需要形成配方推荐或明确 hold 时才调用 `screen_formulations`：
   传入当前候选和完整的结构化 `constraint_records`。旧文本字段用于兼容历史输入，
   新设计任务不能用它们替代结构化条件。
   每项 `claim_verdicts` 只判定本次 `candidates` 中实际提交的候选。候选集合变更时，
   同步更新各断言的候选判定，保持原任务的全部条件。工具返回参数错误后，修复
   指出的字段并重新提交完整请求，不得删去 `constraint_records` 或联合条件来消除报错。
    倍率与循环次数是两种不同测试，分别建立约束：指定 1 C 测试使用
    `{"kind":"c_rate","operator":"==","value":1,"unit":"C"}`；
    100 次循环使用 `{"kind":"minimum_cycles","value":100,"unit":"cycles"}`。
    指定 2.0–4.0 V 测试使用
    `{"kind":"voltage_window","operator":"==","value":[2.0,4.0],"unit":"V"}`。
    若任务要求 0.5 C 和 1 C，各自建立条件。
    双盐配方同时保存 `salts` 与 `salt_concentrations_mol_l`，分别记录各盐浓度；
    `concentration_mol_l` 表示总盐浓度，不得将它归给某一个盐。
    `solvent_ratio_basis` 按原文填写 `mass`、`volume` 或 `molar`；原文未说明时填
    `unknown`。不得把质量比例当成体积比例，或把溶剂比例直接当成包括盐的摩尔组成。
   若本任务已声明 `joint_context_requirements`，每次首次筛选和补证后的重新筛选都必须携带
   同一份 joint-context 合同；除非用户明确修改任务目标，否则不得在 re-screen 时删除、
   放宽 `context_fields` 或改写 `target_context`。runtime 会在字段被意外省略时保留上一版
   显式合同，但 Agent 仍应主动原样传递。
   保留工具原样返回的 `screening_results`、其中的 `criteria_evaluations` 与 `gaps`，
   不得手写分数、validations 或 scores。任何 `failed`、`insufficient_evidence` 或
   `unsupported` 判定都不得在报告中表述为性能已验证。
7. 旧调用方需要动作列表时，可调用 `optimize_formulations`：
   `{"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results,"request":{"task_type":"design","objectives":[目标性能...],"constraints":[用户硬约束...]}}`。
   不得同时传入 `validations` 或 `scores`。该兼容工具只翻译筛选后已经产生的
   `DecisionState`，不会再按 score 独立裁决；若 proposal 为
   `retrieve_more_evidence`，先执行对应的补充检索和重新筛选，再进入报告。
8. `DecisionState` 已达到 `recommend` 或 `hold` 后，必须**立即**调用 `synthesize_design_report`
   生成完整报告，并传入同一份原始 `screening_results`：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","question":用户问题,"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results}}`。
   为提升 `claim_supported_ratio`，请在 `request.claims` 中提交**所有**被 `evidence_chunks` 直接支持的事实声明（`claim_type="fact"`），每条包含 `text`、对应 `chunk_id` 和唯一逐字原文引文 `evidence_quote`（必须从该 chunk 的 `content` 中逐字截取，且只出现一次）。**禁止为凑数量编造 claim**；若当前证据能直接支持的 claim 不足 2 条，应优先通过 `search_literature_chunks` 或 `search_paper_chunks` 补充检索，最多尝试 2 轮；若仍无法找到更多直接支持，则在报告中明确标注“证据不足”，并只提交已被验证的 claim。报告将渲染“已校验事实”小节，避免裁判从自由文本中抽取不被检索上下文支持的论断。
   报告要让使用者能安排下一步工作。用简明中文分别提交配方组成、文献的测试条件与数值、同条件基准配方的结果，并保留逐字引文。比例需说明质量比或体积比；浓度、添加剂用量不得省略或猜测。文献筛选不能写成新配方已由本智能体实验验证。
   当目标是某项性能时，报告必须包含已检索到的该项性能结果，不能只列出温度、
   电极和电压范围等测试设置。不同盐浓度、溶剂比例和添加剂分支的结果分别绑定到
   其配方。不得借用另一分支较好的结果；保留同一分支完整组成与性能已明确的候选，
   不必强求选取数值最高但组成仍缺失的分支。
   `next_steps` 按本次缺口列出具体核查或实验，包括要比较的配方、温度、倍率、电池类型和测量项目；这些是验证计划，不是已取得的结果。即使为 `hold`，也要展示已取得的候选资料、文献结果和暂缓原因，不得只写状态或检索流程。
   对没有数值判据的选材目标，`next_steps` 也要交代其验证状态。例如成本目标
   需要区分文献的成本动机与实际价格比较，不能因筛选通过就宣称全部目标已验证。
   性能类 `claims` 应优先包含与当前候选直接相连的实验结果，少选一般背景介绍。
   **关键纪律**：一旦 `screen_formulations` 返回 `hold` 或 `recommend`，**不得**再尝试重新构建候选、重新检索或输出自由文本；下一动作必须是 `synthesize_design_report`。若状态为 `search`，最多只做一轮补充检索 + 重新筛选，然后必须进入报告。
9. 直接输出报告全文，不得改写或截断。

## 退出纪律

- 不要求无条件调用所有工具；根据用户已有候选和结构化 evidence gaps 选择能力。
- `synthesize_design_report` 是终端编译能力。调用前必须已有终态 `DecisionState`；
  `search` 状态必须先按缺口补证或换候选，不能用固定工具次数代替状态判断。
- `recommend` 只推荐 approved candidates；`hold` 展示已检索的候选资料与文献结果，说明缺口和验证计划，不推荐或排序候选。

## 候选方案纪律

- 候选配方必须来自 KG 结构化证据或文献 chunk；
- 对于"建议组合"（无完整配方直接实验数据），summary 只写组分和证据来源，不写性能声明；
- 性能/效果声明只能绑定到直接支持该声明的 chunk_id；
- 禁止在"证据摘要"里写入未被任何 chunk 直接支持的推断句；无来源支撑的直接删除；
- **直接回答（direct_answer）只给出候选方案标识和最精简组成**，不要包含"已在某温度验证"、"性能最优"、"最有效"等需要跨证据推断的断言；
- 推荐完整配方必须有原文明确的钠盐浓度。若浓度未知，列为待补资料，不得填入
  “参考基准配方”的浓度并作为已有文献验证的配方推荐。

## 推荐/排序纪律

- 排序理由必须逐条绑定到具体 chunk_id，禁止写"C1/C3/C4 无法满足需求"、"某候选明显优于其他"等无直接对比证据的绝对化断言；
- 无直接对比证据时，只陈述各候选的组分、证据来源与评分，不给出相对优劣结论；
- 对"建议组合"的推荐，只能说明其组分和所依据的证据，不得把多篇证据的性能迁移到该组合上。

## 证据摘要纪律

- 配方段落若讨论多种浓度、多个溶剂比例或不同研究，先定位到单一配方的原文。
  不得把某段的浓度、另一配方的溶剂比例和第三个体系的添加剂拼成候选。
  原文工具返回中的数值、温度符号、配方标识和 chunk_id 应原样沿用，
  不得手工改写成另一温度或用整篇论文的共同身份代替相同测试条件。
- 每条 bullet 必须附带 `[chunk_id]`；
- 禁止输出以"【推断】"开头的句子；
- 禁止把多篇证据的性能迁移到某个候选配方上。

## 引用纪律

- 使用 `[chunk_id]` 格式；
- 禁止引用模型参数知识里的文献；
- 单篇报道就写"某文献报道/某体系显示"，不得升格为普适结论。

## KG 质量反馈

检索或分析过程中，若发现以下可疑情况，**必须**调用 `flag_suspicious_kg_item` 记录，供后续离线人工审查与 KG 矫正；不阻塞当前设计流程。

- **实体标签错误**：如 `ionic conductivity` 被标为 `Additive`，`NaPF6` 被标为 `Solvent`；
- **关系方向/语义错误**：如 `SEI DECOMPOSITION::FORMS::FEC`、明显违背化学常识的关系；
- **属性单位或数值异常**：如电导率 `100 mS/cm` 与上下文矛盾、温度单位混用；
- **同名异义**：如 `TMP` 同时指 `trimethyl phosphate` 与 `2,4,6-trimethylpyridine` 而未区分；
- **证据与 KG 矛盾**：chunk 中的明确结论与 KG 检索结果冲突。

记录时尽量提供：item_type（`entity`/`relation`/`property`）、具体名称/ID、问题描述、触发工具、证据 chunk_id。

## 知识沉淀

设计流程全部结束后，调用 `reflect_now` 进行知识反思和 Wiki 沉淀，
将本次设计的关键结论、发现的知识缺口、改进的检索关键词记录到 LLM Wiki，
供下次相似问题时直接检索复用，减少重复检索成本。

additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
I now have a strong candidate set. Let me organize.

Key paper for the no-plating limit: [0036_Lin 2019] — exactly Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 || HC full cell, -20 °C, coin cells, 1 M NaClO4 EC/PC (1:1 vol). No-plating safe capacity 250 mAh/g (anode basis) at -20 °C. Full cell fades fast at -20 °C → electrolyte needs improvement.

Now for electrolyte candidates with -20 °C evidence:
1. NPMV electrolyte: 1.0 M NaClO4 - PC/MB (methyl butyrate) + 1 wt% VC, 1:1 vol ratio [0065_Wan 2025]. PB||HC full cell at -20 °C: 59.48 mAh/g discharge (vs NPV 29.57), 80.0 mAh/g with 78.5% retention after 50 cycles at -20 °C. Ionic conductivity 1.94 mS/cm at -20 °C. Note: cathode is PB (Prussian blue), not NVPF. But the electrolyte is validated with HC anode in full cell at -20 °C. Also NFM||HC coin cells.

2. NaDFOB-G2 (diglyme) electrolyte [0070_Xia 2025]: NFPP electrode 92.7% retention at -20 °C vs 25 °C; also works with Na3V2(PO4)2F3 electrodes (cycling stability over 200 cycles). Has HC anode discussion. This is highly relevant: NVPF-compatible + -20 °C.

3. 1 M NaPF6 PC/EMC [0005_Che 2021]: 82.95% retention at -20 °C, 74.40% at -30, 52.16% at -40. Cathode NFM. EC-based electrolytes almost do not operate below -20 °C.

4. PCMF electrolyte [0142_Du 2026]: PBA||Na? section title says "Wide-temperature electrochemical performance of PBA||Na" — hmm, might be PBA||HC. 89.51% retention after 300 cycles at -20 °C.

5. 0029_Li 2024: NaPF6/DEGDME for HC, low temperature. 247.5 mAh/g after 2000 cycles at 1.0 A/g; "Even at..." need more.

6. NaPF6/diglyme with Na4VP (Na-rich NVP) cathode + HC full cell at -20 °C: 92.3 mAh/g at -20 °C [0264_Liu 2023]. That's NVP not NVPF but same cathode family and gives a UV-temperature series. Actually it's a Na-free-anode full cell — cathode Na4VP + HC anode? Let me check: "the electrochemical performances of hard carbon anode with Na4VP cathode Na-ion full cell". Yes! Na4VP||HC full cell with NaPF6/diglyme, -20 °C → 92.3 mAh/g (based on cathode mass). That's a relevant candidate electrolyte for NVP-family||HC at -20 °C.

7. 0013_Deng 2025: dilute ether-based electrolyte with heterostructured NaF/Na2CO3-rich SEI, HC anode, low-temperature SIBs. Need formulation. Also quasi-solid-state full cells HC//PFSA-Na//NVOPF@rGO — NVOPF = Na3V2O2(PO4)2F? Actually NVOPF is Na3V2O2(PO4)2F, related to NVPF. Hmm, but it's a solid-state system (PFSA-Na membrane) → not relevant electrolyte for liquid.

Focus: The user asks for a design task: "determine a reversible no-plating capacity limit ... while selecting an appropriate electrolyte." So the deliverable: (a) the capacity limit (250 mAh/g anode basis at -20 °C, from Lin 2019, ~80% of RT capacity; plating intervenes around 300 mAh/g), and (b) recommended electrolyte with composition and evidence.

Now, the constraint "candidate must have same-paper evidence for the target cell (NVPF||HC full cell)" is very strict. Let's check which candidates have NVPF||HC full-cell evidence:
- Lin 2019 baseline: 1 M NaClO4 in EC/PC 1:1 vol — NVPF||HC coin cell at -20 °C, BUT fast capacity fading at -20 °C → fails the low-temperature viability claim (no-plating capability in full cell unproven / poor).
- 0023_Hu 2024: dual-anion ether electrolyte, Na3V2(PO4)2F3 cathode, wide temperature; HM-NVPF@CN-BPG at -25 °C gives 98 mAh/g at 0.2 C; full cell with hard carbon anode over 930 cycles at 1C. Need formulation and whether -20 °C full cell data exists. Let me search within that paper.
- 0070_Xia 2025: NaDFOB-G2 with Na3V2(PO4)2F3 electrode cycling stability over 200 cycles (Fig S9) — but at what temperature? And with HC anode?
- 0029_Li 2024: NaPF6/DEGDME — need low-temp details and whether it's full cell.

Let me do focused paper-internal searches for 0023_Hu, 0070_Xia, 0029_Li, and also 0026? Let me also check 0028_Li PEMP electrolyte.

Let's search paper chunks:
- 0023_Hu: "electrolyte composition salt concentration dual anion full cell hard carbon -20 °C"
- 0070_Xia: "NaDFOB diglyme electrolyte concentration hard carbon anode full cell NVPF -20 °C"

Also search literature for more NVPF||HC full cell at low temperature.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0036::plating
evidence_chunks.content: The optical images in Figure S6 clearly indicate the formation of Na metal at the capacity of 350 mAh g-1. Sodium dendrite could be recognized at the capacity of 450 mAh g-1. The above results suggest that sodium plating start to intervene around 300 mAh g-1, and it will be safe to use HC within the capacity of 250 mAh g-1 at -20 °C.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0036::fullcell
evidence_chunks.content: The voltage profiles of Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3/HC full cell consists of a plateau at 4.1 V and sloping regime between 3.6-2.5 V, contributing to an accumulative capacity of 306 mAh g-1 (based on the mass of anode). The energy density is calculated to be 310 Wh kg-1 based on the total weight of cathode and anode, along with an average discharge potential of 3.62 V. It maintains 93.2% and 80.4% of the capacity at room temperature for testing at 0°C and -20°C, respectively. It is worthwhile to mention that the safe capacity for HC working at -20°C is 250 mAh g-1, which is also around 80% of its capacity at room temperature.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0065::fullcell20
evidence_chunks.content: NPMV works well, especially at low temperature, delivering a high discharge capacity of 59.48 mAh g-1 at -20 °C, while a rapid capacity dropping is observed in the NPV electrolyte with only 29.57 mAh g-1.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0065::cycling20
evidence_chunks.content: the PB||HC full cell with the NPMV electrolyte exhibits a high capacity of 80.0 mAh g-1 and a capacity retention of 78.5% after 50 cycles, in sharp contrast to the 35.5 mAh g-1 and 74.5% in the NPV electrolyte.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0065::conductivity
evidence_chunks.content: the NPMV electrolyte delivers the higher values of 1.94 mS cm-1 at -20 °C, 4.89 mS cm-1 at 25 °C, and 11.73 mS cm-1 at 100 °C, compared with 1.14, 4.57, and 10.84 mS cm-1 in the NPV electrolyte.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0029::fullcell
evidence_chunks.content: the full cell also exhibited outstanding performance at -20 °C. Particularly, the full cell maintains a reversible capacity of 75.5 mAh g-1 after 100 cycles at 0.1 A g-1 (Fig. 6c), with the plateau still evident in the discharge/charge profiles (Fig. 6d), corresponding to a high capacity retention of 80.2 %.

the HC electrode can still deliver a high ICE of 60.7 % and a reversible capacity of 257.5 mAh g-1 after 100 cycles at 0.1 A g-1 ... Compared with the maximum capacity (258.9 mAh g-1) obtained during the initial activation, the capacity retention is as high as 99.4 %.
The cell exhibits a reversible specific capacity of 105.5, 105.4, 104.5, 100.3, and 92.3 mAh g-1 at 25, 10, 0, -10, and -20 °C, respectively.
the NFPP electrode with NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte exhibits a capacity retention of 92.7% at -20 °C compared to that at 25 °C. Even at -40 °C, a high capacity retention of 84.8% is achieved.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0070::cond

I now have good numeric evidence. Let me update todos and then decide candidates.

Key facts established:
1. **No-plating limit (exact cell)**: Lin 2019 [0036]: HC at -20 °C: plating starts ~300 mAh/g; safe to use HC within 250 mAh/g at -20 °C, evidenced by in situ/ex situ XRD and Raman + optical images (Fig S6). NVPF||HC full cell: 306 mAh/g (anode basis), 310 Wh/kg, avg 3.62 V; RT stable; at -20 °C full cell shows fast capacity fading due to increased resistance and continuous Na consumption → electrolyte optimization required. Electrolyte = 1 M NaClO4 in EC/PC (1:1 vol), CR2032 coin cells, NVPF:HC weight ratio 2.5, glass fiber separator.

So the answer to "reversible no-plating capacity limit at -20 °C" = 250 mAh g⁻¹ based on anode (HC) mass ≈ 80% of RT HC capacity; with the caveat that this limit was determined in HC half-cells with 1 M NaClO4 EC/PC.

2. **Electrolyte candidates with -20 °C evidence in HC-containing full cells**:
   - C1 baseline NaClO4 EC/PC (Lin) — same cell, but fades at -20 °C.
   - NPMV: 1.0 M NaClO4-PC/MB + 1 wt% VC (1:1 vol) [0065]: PB||HC full cell at -20 °C: 59.48 mAh/g discharge; 80.0 mAh/g after 50 cycles with 78.5% retention; ionic conductivity 1.94 mS/cm at -20 °C. Note: 80.0 mAh/g capacity with 78.5% retention after 50 cycles at -20 °C — presumably the initial capacity was ~102 mAh/g. Hmm, careful: "exhibits a high capacity of 80.0 mAh/g and a capacity retention of 78.5% after 50 cycles". So 80 mAh/g retained with 78.5% retention means initial ~101.9. OK.
   - G1: 1.0 M NaPF6 in DME [0029]: NVP/C||HC full cell at -20 °C: 75.5 mAh/g after 100 cycles at 0.1 A/g, 80.2% retention; HC half-cell 257.5 mAh/g at -20 °C (99.4% retention). Cathode = NVP/C.
   - NaPF6/diglyme 1 M [0264]: Na4VP||HC full cell: 92.3 mAh/g at -20 °C at C/5; avg CE 95% at -20 °C. Also explicitly: Na plating accelerated when charge rate > 1C.
   - NaDFOB-G2 1 M [0070]: HC//NFPP pouch at -20 °C, 0.2C cycling; NVPF electrode compatible (200 cycles, Fig S9).

Now the design task requires selecting an electrolyte for the NVPF||HC full cell at -20 °C. Constraint: NVPF cathode (high voltage ~4.1-4.3 V vs Na). Ether electrolytes have limited oxidative stability — but NaDFOB-G2 has >5.2 V oxidation potential, and the paper explicitly shows compatibility with Na3V2(PO4)2F3 electrodes. Hmm, that's a strong candidate. But its -20 °C full cell evidence is with NFPP cathode (3.1-3.5 V class). Actually wait: NFPP = Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 or Na3Fe2(PO4)P2O7.

Also candidate with -20 °C HC full cell and NVP-family cathode: 1 M NaPF6 in diglyme [0264] with Na4VP cathode (3.35 V avg) — and its LS: base ester electrolyte EC/DEC had poor CE with Na metal.

Hmm, given the process, `query_formulation_space` must be called to get candidates. Let me consider what to feed it.

Actually, let me reconsider the design target. The user's core ask: "determine a reversible no-plating capacity limit for a Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3||hard-carbon sodium-ion full cell at -20 C while selecting an appropriate electrolyte."

Deliverable: The no-plating capacity limit (250 mAh/g on anode basis at -20 °C, from the exact-cell study) + an electrolyte selection with evidence.

For electrolyte selection, the appropriate criteria: (1) tested at -20 °C; (2) used with hard carbon anode in a full cell; (3) compatible with NVPF-class cathode (high voltage ~4.1 V); (4) enables reversible cycling without plating.

Candidates:
- E1: 1.0 M NaDFOB in diglyme (G2) [0070_Xia2025] — HC//NFPP pouch cell, -20 °C cycling; compatible with Na3V2(PO4)2F3 electrode; high oxidation potential >5.2 V; conductivity 0.99 mS/cm at -40 °C. Formulation explicit: 1 M NaDFOB, diglyme, no additive needed (own film-forming).
- E2: 1.0 M NaPF6 in DME (G1) [0029_Li2024] — NVP/C||HC full cell at -20 °C 75.5 mAh/g, 80.2% retention; HC half cell at -20 °C 257.5 mAh/g.
- E3: 1.0 M NaClO4-PC/MB + 1 wt% VC (NPMV) [0065_Wan2025] — PB||HC full cell at -20 °C.
- E4: 1 M NaPF6 in diglyme [0264_Liu2023] — Na4VP||HC full cell at -20 °C 92.3 mAh/g.
- E5: baseline 1 M NaClO4 in EC/PC (1:1 vol) [0036_Lin2019] — exact NVPF||HC cell but fades at -20 °C.

Now, the strict requirement "candidate_same_paper" evidence for the electrode pair NVPF||HC. Only E5 has that. So under strict screening, E1-E4 may fail the "NVPF cathode + hard carbon + -20 °C in same study" joint constraint.

Hmm, this is the crux: the design decision becomes a HOLD with a clear rationale: the exact cell (NVPF||HC) at -20 °C has only been reported with the baseline carbonate electrolyte (which fades), while improved low-temperature electrolytes (ether-based) have been demonstrated in other Na-ion full cells with HC anodes. So we can hold and give a validation plan, OR recommend the electrolyte whose high-voltage compatibility with NVPF is documented.

I think the honest, evidence-based outcome is likely **hold** for recommending a specific electrolyte to the exact NVPF||HC cell at -20 °C, since no retrieved study reports an improved electrolyte in that exact cell at -20 °C with no-plating verification. But the report must still present: the no-plating limit (250 mAh/g anode basis) and candidate electrolytes with their actual test conditions.

Hmm, but hold might be too conservative. Let me reconsider: the task says "while selecting an appropriate electrolyte". The screening tool decides. Let me set up constraints honestly and let the DecisionState decide.

Let me think about what constraints to declare:
1. `temp-target`: temperature <= -20 °C (evidence_claim? no, temperature kind). required_evidence_scope: candidate_same_paper.

7. field_presence: concentration_mol_l, solvents.

Hmm, but constraint 3 (NVPF cathode, same paper) would fail for E1-E4. Then DecisionState would be hold or search. Given the skill says: "若当前候选仍不能满足目标，按缺口与完整目标检索其他候选" — search. We've done that; the literature genuinely has no NVPF||HC + improved electrolyte at -20 °C.

Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider whether there is such a paper. Let me search specifically for "Na3V2(PO4)2F3 hard carbon full cell low temperature electrolyte" variants, e.g., 0412? Let me do one more focused search on NVPF||HC full cell at low temperature with electrolyte engineering. Actually I did search "Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 hard carbon full cell -20 °C" and got Lin 2019 top. Let me also try resolving "/Na3V2(PO4)2F3||HC" and 0035_Liang (Mo-NVPF@rGO at -20 °C).

Let me check 0035_Liang: "A General Strategy for Electrolyte-Interphase Reconstruction via Molybdenum-Driven Catalytic Engineering" with NVPF@rGO cathode and Mo-NVPF@rGO tested under -20 °C. That could be a full-cell with hard carbon? Let me search that paper.

Also 0041_Liu: "Single-Atom Nb-N4 Sites Regulate Hard Carbon Interface for Ultrastable and Low-Temperature Sodium-Ion..." — HC anode low temperature.

Let me do these two paper-internal searches plus one multiview for NVPF||HC full cell low temperature.

Actually — I should be efficient. Let me do these 3 in parallel:
- search_paper_chunks 0035_Liang: "NVPF full cell hard carbon -20 °C electrolyte capacity"
- search_paper_chunks 0041_Liu: "hard carbon full cell low temperature electrolyte NaPF6 diglyme cathode -20 °C"
- search_literature_multiview: ["Na3V2(PO4)2F3 cathode hard carbon anode full cell low temperature electrolyte -20 °C", "sodium plating hard carbon anode low temperature ether electrolyte full cell no plating capacity limit"]

Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The cells underwent a formation process at a 0.1 C rate, as shown in the formation curves in Figure S1. The charge and discharge curves of both cells were nearly identical. Subsequent EIS analysis after formation revealed that cells with the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN exhibited lower resistance (Figure 1a), indicating that the PFPN additive effectively reduces interfacial resistance in the cells.

The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b). additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
Excellent — E3 (NaDFOB-G2) is very strong quantitative evidence: Ah-level HC//NFPP pouch cell discharge capacities 0.985, 0.884, 1.06 Ah at -20, -40, 60 °C (0.1 C), = 95.7%, 85.9%, 103% retention; 80% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C; -20 °C cycling (0.2 C) over hundreds of cycles.

However the cathode there is NFPP, not NVPF. But: "Both the Na3V2(PO4)3 and Na3V2(PO4)2F3 electrodes show high cycling stability over 200 cycles" with NaDFOB-G2, and oxidation potential >5.2 V. Also, NaDFOB-G2 beats NaPF6-G2 at -20 and -40 °C.

I didn't find the concentration for 0041_Liu's NaPF6-DME (searched twice). Hmm — the paper says "NaPF6-DME electrolyte" — no explicit concentration retrieved. So E1 (NaPF6-DME) lacks explicit salt concentration → per skill, cannot be a fully recommended formulation (concentration unknown → 待补资料).

Now which candidates do I pass to query_formulation_space and screen?

Given the skill requires `query_formulation_space` (required: true) with evidence_chunks (up to 12 most relevant), I'll pass the retrieved chunks and target conditions.

Candidate list for the space:
1. E-A: 1 M NaClO4 in EC/PC (1:1 vol) — Lin 2019 baseline, NVPF||HC coin.
2. E-B: 1.0 M NaClO4 in PC/MB (1:1 vol) + 1 wt% VC (NPMV) — Wan 2025.
3. E-C: 1.0 M NaPF6 in DME (G1) — Li 2024.
4. E-D: 1 M NaPF6 in diglyme — Liu 2023.
5. E-E: 1.0 M NaDFOB in diglyme (G2) — Xia 2025.
6. E-F: NaPF6-DME (concentration not found) — Liu 2025 (NVPF||Nb-NC at -20 °C) — hmm, concentration unknown. Might be excluded or listed as gap.
7. E-G: 1 M NaPF6 PC:EMC:FEC 50:47:3 vol + 2 wt% DDTD + 10 wt% PFPN — Zhang 2025 (with anti-plating evidence at 0 °C, NFM-HC pouch).

That's a lot. The tool may return candidates itself. Let me call query_formulation_space with target conditions and preferences, plus evidence_chunks. Then enrich if needed, then screen.

Let me now define constraint_records carefully:

User requirements:
- Cell: Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 cathode || hard carbon anode, full cell.
- Temperature: -20 °C.
- Deliverable: reversible no-plating capacity limit (a quantitative determination) + electrolyte selection.

Constraints:
1. `temp-minus20`: kind temperature, operator "<=", value -20, unit °C, required_evidence_scope "candidate_same_paper", can_replan true.
   Hmm — should it be "<=" or "=="? The user says "at -20 C". Using "<=" -20 allows -40 °C tests to pass (e.g., NaDFOB tested at both). Given the paper tested at -20 °C explicitly for all main candidates, either works. The skill's example uses "<=". I'll use "<=" to include the -20 °C data point. Actually careful: temperature "<=" -20 with candidate evidence at -20 exactly → passes. Data only at -40 or 0 °C would fail. I'll use "<=".

2. `anode-hard-carbon`: kind electrode_material, evidence_terms ["hard carbon", "hard-carbon", "HC"], candidate_same_paper.

3. `cathode-nvpf`: kind electrode_material, evidence_terms ["Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3", "NVPF", "Na3V2(PO4)2F3", "sodium vanadium fluorophosphate"], candidate_same_paper. 

Hmm — this will fail for most candidates. But it's a user requirement (the cell has an NVPF cathode). Actually, the user says the cell is NVPF||HC. To select an electrolyte for that cell, we need NVPF compatibility. Should the requirement be "the electrolyte was tested with an NVPF cathode" in the same paper? That is a reasonable reading: the electrolyte must be validated with this cathode chemistry. Yes, I'll include it. It's a user-given electrode material requirement.

4. `cell-full`: kind cell_configuration, evidence_terms ["full cell", "full battery", "pouch cell", "coin cell", "Ah-level"]. candidate_same_paper.

Hmm, careful: "coin cell" alone would match half-cells too. Let me use terms: ["full cell", "full cells", "full battery", "pouch cell", "pouch cells"].

5. `no-plating-claim`: kind evidence_claim. claim: "该候选电解液在 -20 °C 下用于硬碳负极电池时，未观测到钠金属析出（析钠被抑制）". claim_verdicts per candidate.

Which candidates can support this? 
- E-A (Lin, 1 M NaClO4 EC/PC): supported — HC within 250 mAh/g at -20 °C is safe without Na plating (in situ XRD + Raman + optical images at 350 mAh/g show Na metal). Quote from 0036::sec6::child12. Verdict: supported.
- E-E (NaDFOB-G2): no -20 °C plating statement. not_found.
- E-G (PFPN): "effectively preventing sodium plating" but at 0 °C / 30 °C, not -20 °C. Hmm, the claim says "在 -20 °C 下". So not_found for -20 °C. Maybe phrase the claim as "该候选电解液被报道抑制硬碳负极上的钠析出" without -20 °C? But the user's question is -20 °C. Better: phrase claim = "在该候选电解液的全电池 -20 °C 测试中，未观测到钠析出（可逆容量下无析钠）" and mark not_found where absent.
- E-C (NaPF6/DME, 0029): not stated. not_found.
- E-B (NPMV): not stated. not_found.
- E-D (NaPF6/diglyme, 0264): "the deposition of Na metal is accelerated when the charge rate increases beyond 1C" — that's about Na-free-anode cells with excess Na metal in carbon host; it's a statement that plating happens beyond 1C. Not exactly a no-plating claim at -20 °C. not_found.

evidence.text: In summary, a hard carbon material for NIBs is fabricated from low-cost biomass waste using a facile two-step thermal treatment. Compared to direct high-temperature carbonization, the pre-treatment at a medium temperature is beneficial to avoiding the selfactivation effect of impurities. An appropriate surface area and pore size distribution are obtained, enabling a stable capacity of around 300 mAh g $^{-1}$ . It also shows excellent performance at a temperature as low as -20 °C. A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C, as evidenced by in situ XRD and Raman tests. As-prepared HC also delivers stable performance in the full cell coupling with a $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ cathode, demonstrated an energy density of 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ (based on the total weight of electrode) with decent cyclic stability at room temperature. evidence.text:
3. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b).

In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The cells were galvanostatic charged/discharged with a LAND 2001 CT battery test system (Wuhan, China) under various voltage ranges and current rates.

A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C, as evidenced by in situ XRD and Raman tests. evidence.text:
3. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b).

evidence.text: In summary, the incorporation of PFPN as an electrolyte additive has successfully led to significant enhancements in both the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries and the flame retardancy of the electrolyte. The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a SEI layer rich in P and N elements

- c1-1M-NaClO4-EC-PC：候选配方与文献全电池所用电解质完全一致，且原文给出了 -20 °C 无析钠容量上限 250 mAh g^-1 的可转移依据，评估问题已可回答；但同一文献明确指出该电解质下全电池在 -20 °C 快速衰减并需优化电解质以构建稳定 SEI，故不应将当前无添加剂的 1 M NaClO4/EC-PC 作为低温全电池的推荐电解质，暂缓推荐。
- c1-1M-NaClO4-EC-PC：候选电解质在 -20 °C 支持目标全电池稳定可逆循环：原文报告采用该电解质的全电池在 -20 °C 出现快速容量衰减，归因于低温阻抗增大与 Na 持续消耗，并明确呼吁未来优化电解质体系以构建稳定 SEI，构成对该候选电解质低温全电池适用性的反证。

Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional lithium-ion batteries, thanks to the abundant sodium reserves, low cost, and reliable safety performance $[1]$ . As a key component of SIBs, anode materials are crucial for determining the overall sodium storage performance. However, the larger ionic radius of $Na^{+}$ (0.102 nm) compared to $Li^{+}$ (0.076 nm) leads to sluggish transport kinetics and severe volume expansion during sodiation, resulting in issues such as unsatisfactory energy density, sluggish redox kinetics, and inadequate rate capability $[2]$ . Furthermore, conventional graphite anode materials are difficult to form stable intercalation compounds with $Na^{+}$ , making it hard to achieve efficient $Na^{+}$ storage, which limits their application in SIBs $[3-5]$ . Therefore, researchers are committed to developing new high-performance anode materials suitable for $Na^{+}$ insertion/extraction to meet the demands of large-scale energy storage systems and electric vehicle applications. Among various anode materials, hard carbon (HC), with its unique vortex-layered graphene stacking structure and internal microporous network, provides abundant $Na^{+}$ storage sites and exhibits an extremely low operating potential window, making it an ideal candidate for high-energy-density SIBs anodes $[6-9]$ . Nevertheless, the inherent instability of the HC/electrolyte interface results in low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), coupled with slow ion diffusion kinetics and limited cycling stability, which severely hinders its widespread application $[10-12]$ .

To overcome the aforementioned technical bottlenecks, researchers have employed various strategies to enhance the electrochemical performance of HC, including accelerating the $Na^{+}$ kinetics during intercalation/deintercalation in graphite-like regions by regulating interlayer spacing; introducing heteroatoms (N, S, F, B, etc.) or functional groups to provide more surface active adsorption sites; and adjusting specific surface area while passivating defects to enhance initial ICE [13, 14]. Overall, these strategies aim to balance the energy barriers for $Na^{+}$ adsorption and transport by regulating the local microstructure, which is typically achieved through precise precursor selection and treatment. Introduction
Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) have been an attractive alternative for the post lithium-ion battery due to the wide abundance and low cost of sodium resources. $^{[1-7]}$ The electrolyte is known as the “blood” of SIBs and interacts closely with the cathode and anode. $^{[8-13]}$ The electrolyte not only plays an important role in regulating the properties of the electrode/electrolyte interface but also has a crucial impact on the battery performance, including reversible capacity, rate capability, cycling stability, high and low-temperature performance, and safety. $^{[14-20]}$ Therefore, it is very important to explore advanced electrolytes to achieve high-performance SIBs.

The sodium salt is the main component of electrolytes of SIBs, which directly determines the electrochemical characteristics of electrolytes. $^{[21-23]}$ At present, the commonly used sodium salts are mainly sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_{6}$ ), sodium perchlorate (NaClO $_{4}$ ), sodium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (NaTFSI), and sodium

bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI). $^{[24-27]}$ However, all these salts have shortcomings for large-scale application. For example, $NaClO_{4}$ is very explosive and its adsorbed $H_{2}O$ is too difficult to dry out. $^{[28]}$ $NaPF_{6}$ is toxic and expensive, easy to decompose at elevated temperatures and under humidity. $^{[5,14]}$ The NaTFSI and NaFSI are of high cost, and the $TFSI^{-}$ (or $FSI^{-}$ ) anion in NaTFSI (or NaFSI) has a corrosive effect on the aluminum foil collector. $^{[8]}$ Thus, it is of great significance to explore advanced salts to promote the wide applicability of SIBs. Sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB), which has non-localized electrons in the structure and weak bonds between sodium-ions and anions, has shown fascinating properties, such as high conductivity, compatibility with a variety of solvents, and own film-forming characteristics with no need for film-forming additives. $^{[14,29,30]}$ However, the use of NaDFOB as a single salt for electrolytes and their compatibility with different SIB electrodes have rarely been reported. One reason may be the concern of its high cost as the current synthesis process for NaDFOB is complex, dangerous, and costly. $^{[29]}$

Miaomiao Xia, Hui Chen, Zhenxu Zheng, Qingfei Meng, $^{*}$ Along Zhao, Xiaoyang Chen, Xinping Ai, Yongjin Fang, $^{*}$ and Yuliang Cao $^{*}$

Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising alternative for next-generation energy storage solutions, driven by the economic and environmental benefits of abundant sodium resources. A pivotal aspect of SIB advancement is the development of advanced electrolytes, which remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a facile and scalable synthesis method for low-cost sodium-difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) is reported and explored its application as a standalone electrolyte salt for SIBs. The NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, solvent compatibility, and the unique capacity to form a dense, robust solid-electrolyte interphase layer on electrode surfaces. As a result, the $\mathrm{Na_{4}Fe_{3}(PO_{4})_{2}P_{2}O_{7}}$ (NFPP) cathode with NaDFOB-based electrolyte exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability with a remarkable capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles. Furthermore, an Ah-level hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell using NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte shows an impressive cycle life of 500 cycles, coupled with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%. The pouch cells also maintain superior electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range from -40 to 60 °C, showcasing the electrolyte's versatility. additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
The supplementary retrieval confirms:
1. 0029_Li's full cell cathode: "full-cell tests were conducted using NVP/C as the cathode" with "X-ray diffraction pattern exhibits diffraction peaks indicative of its NASICON structure" — so it's Na3V2(PO4)3/C (NASICON NVP), NOT NVPF (Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 has a different structure — it's also NASICON-type actually, but the paper says NVP/C). So cathode identity ≠ Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 confirmed negative. Good — this resolves the reviewer's gap for c3: NVP/C is NVP (NASICON), not NVPF.
Also no plating detection anywhere in 0029.

2. 0041: no plating detection found.

3. 0070: no plating detection.

4. New relevant: 0064_Tao 2023 "Tailoring solid-electrolyte interphase and solvation structure for subzero temperature fast-charging..." — full cell with Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP) cathode and CF-1400 hard carbon-ish anode, ether electrolyte 1M NaPF6-diglyme stabilized below 4.0 V, subzero temperature. That's a new candidate electrolyte with subzero full cell evidence. Hmm — could add as a candidate. But it's the same class as c4. And a new ether electrolyte paper 0009_Cui 2025 (ultraweakly solvating electrolyte for cold-resistant SIBs), 0073_Yang 2023 (entropy-driven solvation low-temperature SIB), 0047_Lv (μ-Sn anode).

Given the reviewer's gaps and my bounded-round allowance (one supplementary retrieval + re-screen), I should now decide: add 0064_Tao as a new candidate (ether, subzero, hard carbon-type anode, NVP cathode) and re-screen with the same constraints. But is it worth it? It adds another ether candidate that also lacks plating-limit evidence. The core conclusion remains: no study in the retrieved corpus provides a -20 °C no-plating capacity limit for NVPF||HC with any electrolyte other than the baseline, and the baseline demonstrably fails at -20 °C.

Rather than expand endlessly, the reviewer's second-round instruction: "请围绕这些实际缺口补取原文或更换候选后重新筛选". I did supplementary retrieval. Now re-screen: I should update claim verdicts to reflect the new evidence (c3's cathode identity now known to be NVP/C NASICON → confirmed not NVPF... well, careful: NVP/C is Na3V2(PO4)3/C. The reviewer asked to "confirm that the 'NVP/C' cathode corresponds to Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3" — the new evidence shows the cathode is NVP/C with NASICON structure, i.e., Na3V2(PO4)3/C, so identity with Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 is refuted/not confirmed. Actually, careful: Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 is also described as NASICON-like... but the paper explicitly calls it NVP/C with 3.3 V plateau and 101.6 mAh/g; NVPF has ~3.8-4.1 V plateau and ~120-130 mAh/g. So the cathode in 0029 is NVP (phosphate), not NVPF (fluorophosphate). I'll add the cathode-composition evidence chunk to c3 and record a verdict that the cathode identity is different.

Let me update candidate c3's evidence (add sec5::child20 and sec5::child21) and re-screen with the same constraints plus updated verdicts. Also maybe add a new candidate c8 from Tao 2023 (1 M NaPF6-diglyme, CF-1400||NVP full cell, subzero). Hmm, its formulation detail: "The ether electrolyte (1M NaPF6-diglyme) can be stabilized below 4.0 V, sufficient for NVP redox reactions". Temperature: "subzero temperature fast-charging" — need actual -20 °C? The query says subzero. I'd need more info; and it doesn't add a plating limit. I'll skip adding it to keep the round bounded — but I should mention it in next_steps as an additional candidate for future assessment. Decision: re-screen with the same 7 candidates, same constraints, same joint contract, with:
- c3 verdicts updated: for the cathode-identity claim, now refuted with the NVP/C NASICON evidence; also add "no plating detection" remains not_found.

evidence.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0
evidence.paper_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt
evidence.text: Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5.

evidence.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child12
evidence.paper_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt
evidence.text: The optical images in Figure S6 clearly indicate the formation of Na metal at the capacity of $350\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . Sodium dendrite could be recognized at the capacity of $450\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . The above results suggest that sodium plating start to intervene around $300\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ , and it will be safe to use HC within the capacity of $250\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The performance of the electrode is not only affected by the active materials but also governed by the other components such as electrolyte and binder. It has been demonstrated by Palacín et al. the importance of electrolyte formulation for the stable performance of HC at low temperature. $^{[21]}$ The binder plays a vital role in maintaining the structural integrity, but its effect under low temperature is not clear yet

evidence.paper_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt
evidence.text: The voltage profiles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell consists of a plateau at 4.1 V and sloping regime between 3.6-2.5 V, contributing to an accumulative capacity of 306 mAh g $^{-1}$ (based on the mass of anode). The energy density is calculated to be 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ based on the total weight of cathode and anode, along with an average discharge potential of 3.62 V. A stable cyclic performance similar to that in half-cell is achieved at $25^{\circ}$ C, as indicated by full cell F1 in Figure 5b. Ulteriorly, we tested the behavior of full cell under low temperature. Firstly, the performance of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ half-cell at 0°C and -20°C are measured and given in Figure S7a and S7b. The reversible capacity decreases with lowering the temperature. It maintains 93.2% and 80.4% of the capacity at room temperature for testing at 0°C and -20°C, respectively. Nevertheless, cyclic stability is kept. It is worthwhile to mention that the safe capacity for HC working at -20°C is 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ , which is also around 80% of its capacity at room temperature. Therefore, there is no need to change the mass ratio of the cathode and anode in the full cell for operating at low temperature.

evidence.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec7::child0
evidence.paper_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt
evidence.text: In summary, a hard carbon material for NIBs is fabricated from low-cost biomass waste using a facile two-step thermal treatment. Compared to direct high-temperature carbonization, the pre-treatment at a medium temperature is beneficial to avoiding the selfactivation effect of impurities. An appropriate surface area and pore size distribution are obtained, enabling a stable capacity of around 300 mAh g $^{-1}$ . It also shows excellent performance at a temperature as low as -20 °C. A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C, as evidenced by in situ XRD and Raman tests. As-prepared HC also delivers stable performance in the full cell coupling with a $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ cathode, demonstrated an energy density of 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ (based on the total weight of electrode) with decent cyclic stability at room temperature. Nevertheless, the full cell shows a fast capacity fading at -20 °C due to both the increased resistance and continuous consumption of Na ions. It calls for building stable SEI under low temperature in future studies.

evidence.text: Varying-Temperature Electrochemical Performance. Furthermore, the potential of the NPMV electrolyte for practical application in a wide-temperature sodium-ion full cell is investigated. First, Figure 5a exhibits the varying-temperature ionic conductivity, where the NPMV electrolyte delivers the higher values of 1.94 mS cm $^{-1}$ at -20 °C, 4.89 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 25 °C, and 11.73 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 100 °C, compared with 1.14, 4.57, and 10.84 mS cm $^{-1}$ in the NPV electrolyte. The varying-temperature electrochemical performance of PB||HC full cells with NPV and NPMV electrolytes is exhibited in Figure 5b, where the charging process is operated at 25 °C and the discharging process over a temperature range from 100 to -20 °C. Much higher capacities are observed in the electrolyte with the MB cosolvent, with 118.34 vs. 94.03 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 100 °C and 92.28 vs. 71.98 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 25 °C. And NPMV works well, especially at low temperature, delivering a high discharge capacity of 59.48 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -20 °C, while a rapid capacity dropping is observed in the NPV electrolyte with only 29.57 mAh g $^{-1}$ .

evidence.text:
3. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b).

evidence.chunk_id: 0083_Zhang 等 - 2025 - Revisiting Interfacial Enhancement Effects of Fluorinated Cyclophosphazene in Practical Sodium-Ion B::sec4::child0
evidence.paper_id: 0083_Zhang 等 - 2025 - Revisiting Interfacial Enhancement Effects of Fluorinated Cyclophosphazene in Practical Sodium-Ion B
evidence.text: In summary, the incorporation of PFPN as an electrolyte additive has successfully led to significant enhancements in both the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries and the flame retardancy of the electrolyte. The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a SEI layer rich in P and N elements on the electrode surface. The SEI layer is thinner and possesses superior kinetic properties compared to the baseline, effectively preventing sodium plating and enhancing the cycle life.

evidence.text: Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5.

evidence.text: The optical images in Figure S6 clearly indicate the formation of Na metal at the capacity of $350\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . Sodium dendrite could be recognized at the capacity of $450\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . The above results suggest that sodium plating start to intervene around $300\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ , and it will be safe to use HC within the capacity of $250\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The performance of the electrode is not only affected by the active materials but also governed by the other components such as electrolyte and binder. It has been demonstrated by Palacín et al. the importance of electrolyte formulation for the stable performance of HC at low temperature.

Notably, the ionic conductivity of NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte still maintains 0.99 mS cm $^{-1}$ at -40 °C, much higher than that of the 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -G2 (0.27 mS cm $^{-1}$ , Figure S2, Supporting Information).

evidence.text: Notably, the NFPP electrode with NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte exhibits a capacity retention of 92.7% at -20 °C compared to that at 25 °C. Even at -40 °C, a high capacity retention of 84.8% is achieved (Figure 2g,h). Moreover, the NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte works well with other cathode materials. Both the $\mathrm{Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}}$ and $\mathrm{Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{2}F_{3}}$ electrodes show high cycling stability over 200 cycles (Figures S8 and S9, Supporting Information). Additionally, the compatibility of the NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte with the hard carbon (HC) anode is also evaluated.

evidence.text: An Ah-level HC//NFPP pouch cells were further assembled to test the feasibility of the practical application of the NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte. evidence.text: As presented in Figure 2c, NaPF $_{6}$ exhibits a relatively low HOMO energy level, indicating its strong stability. evidence.text: For the baseline electrolyte, we employed an electrolyte formulation with certain engineering application value based on prior research conducted by our group. $^{30}$ The specific formulation is as follows: 16.7954 g of NaPF $_{6}$ was dissolved in a 100 mL solvent mixture comprising propylene carbonate (PC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) in a volume ratio of 50:47:3, supplemented with 2 wt % 1,3,2-dioxathiolane-2,2-dioxide (DTD) as an additive. The optimized electrolytes were prepared by adding an appropriate amount of the PFPN additive.

evidence.chunk_id: 0083_Zhang 等 - 2025 - Revisiting Interfacial Enhancement Effects of Fluorinated Cyclophosphazene in Practical Sodium-Ion B::sec3
evidence.paper_id: 0083_Zhang 等 - 2025 - Revisiting Interfacial Enhancement Effects of Fluorinated Cyclophosphazene in Practical Sodium-Ion B
evidence.text: Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d).

evidence.chunk_id: 0083_Zhang 等 - 2025 - Revisiting Interfacial Enhancement Effects of Fluorinated Cyclophosphazene in Practical Sodium-Ion B::sec4::child0
evidence.paper_id: 0083_Zhang 等 - 2025 - Revisiting Interfacial Enhancement Effects of Fluorinated Cyclophosphazene in Practical Sodium-Ion B
evidence.text: The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a SEI layer rich in P and N elements on the electrode surface. The SEI layer is thinner and possesses superior kinetic properties compared to the baseline, effectively preventing sodium plating and enhancing the cycle life.

candidates.rationale: 工程化碳酸酯基准配方 + 10 wt% PFPN，报告抑制硬碳负极钠析出并提升低温循环，但低温数据最低为 0 °C。

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0
evidence_chunks.content: Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5. The cells were galvanostatic charged/discharged with a LAND 2001 CT battery test system (Wuhan, China) under various voltage ranges and current rates. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out on a VMP system (Biologic S.A., Claix, France).

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child12
evidence_chunks.content: The optical images in Figure S6 clearly indicate the formation of Na metal at the capacity of $350\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . Sodium dendrite could be recognized at the capacity of $450\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . The above results suggest that sodium plating start to intervene around $300\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ , and it will be safe to use HC within the capacity of $250\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The performance of the electrode is not only affected by the active materials but also governed by the other components such as electrolyte and binder. It has been demonstrated by Palacín et al. the importance of electrolyte formulation for the stable performance of HC at low temperature. $^{[21]}$ The binder plays a vital role in maintaining the structural integrity, but its effect under low temperature is not clear yet

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child16
evidence_chunks.content: The voltage profiles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell consists of a plateau at 4.1 V and sloping regime between 3.6-2.5 V, contributing to an accumulative capacity of 306 mAh g $^{-1}$ (based on the mass of anode). The energy density is calculated to be 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ based on the total weight of cathode and anode, along with an average discharge potential of 3.62 V. A stable cyclic performance similar to that in half-cell is achieved at $25^{\circ}$ C, as indicated by full cell F1 in Figure 5b. Ulteriorly, we tested the behavior of full cell under low temperature. Firstly, the performance of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ half-cell at 0°C and -20°C are measured and given in Figure S7a and S7b. The reversible capacity decreases with lowering the temperature. It maintains 93.2% and 80.4% of the capacity at room temperature for testing at 0°C and -20°C, respectively. Nevertheless, cyclic stability is kept. It is worthwhile to mention that the safe capacity for HC working at -20°C is 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ , which is also around 80% of its capacity at room temperature. Therefore, there is no need to change the mass ratio of the cathode and anode in the full cell for operating at low temperature.

## 配方筛选结果
已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。

### 候选资料：c1-1M-NaClO4-EC-PC（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaClO4；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaClO4：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, PC；溶剂比例（体积）：EC=0.5, PC=0.5。
- 配方原文 [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0]：Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5. The cells were galvanostatic charged/discharged with a LAND 2001 CT battery test system (Wuhan, China) under various voltage ranges and current rates. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out on a VMP system (Biologic S.A., Claix, France).

ranges. $^{20}$ Moreover, a wide liquid range of ca. 187 °C is also represented in the MB solvent, much higher than that of other carboxylic esters, demonstrating its application potential in wide-temperature batteries (Figure 1d).
